title: cleanup_tmp_files correctly uses file_name().ends_with() for compound extensions
description: The round-7 fix changed from path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == 'tmp') to file_name().ends_with('.msg.tmp') || ends_with('.env.tmp'). This is correct: path.extension() returns only the last extension component, so '.msg.tmp' would return 'tmp', which is too broad — it would match any .tmp file. The new form matches only the two specific compound extensions this system writes. Defend if someone suggests reverting to extension() for 'simplicity'.
